content.title: About
content.content: Coffee is a beverage made from roasted and ground seeds of the coffee plant (genus Coffea). The market offers two main types: brewed (ground) coffee and instant coffee. Brewed coffee retains a richer aroma and flavor, while instant coffee is convenient for quick preparation and storage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coffee is the second most traded commodity in the world after oil.
There are over 100 species of coffee plants, but Arabica and Robusta dominate commercial production.
The first coffeehouse opened in Istanbul in 1555.
Caffeine in coffee stimulates the central nervous system, increasing alertness and concentration.
Instant coffee was invented in the early 20th century and became popular during World War II.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols such as chlorogenic acid that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cognitive function
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption is linked to improved memory, attention, and a lower risk of dementia.

items.title: Boosts metabolism
items.content: Caffeine can increase metabolic rate, aiding calorie burning.

items.title: May reduce risk of certain diseases
items.content: Studies associate regular coffee intake with lower incidence of Parkinson’s disease, type 2 diabetes, and some cancers.

items.title: Enhances physical performance
items.content: Caffeine raises adrenaline levels, which can improve athletic endurance.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat with excessive intake.

items.title: Increased stomach acidity
items.content: Coffee can aggravate gastritis and reflux symptoms in susceptible people.

items.title: Pregnancy considerations
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit caffeine to about 200 mg per day (roughly 1–2 cups).

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of stimulants and diminish the efficacy of sedatives.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Brewed coffee is prepared with hot (not boiling) water at 90–96 °C using methods such as drip, espresso, or French press. Instant coffee is simply dissolved in hot water. Milk, cream, sugar, or spices can be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Ground coffee is best used within 2–3 weeks after opening, while whole beans stay fresh up to 2 months. Instant coffee has a longer shelf life but also requires a dry environment.
